summary: Iteration 64 — Verified link-cascade delete behavior across invoices, bills, and transactions. All 8 pytest cases passed on the deployed backend (client@axiom.ai / company 540fbc73). Confirmed: (1) DELETE invoice/bill removes linked auto-payments and clears txn back-refs, returning {payments_deleted, transactions_cleared}. (2) DELETE txn with linked_payment_id reverses balance impact on doc (invoice paid→sent w/ balance_due restored; bill paid→open w/ balance_due restored) and deletes the payment. (3) Idempotency verified — deleting docs/txns with no linked payments returns payments_deleted=0. (4) Reports downstream stay consistent: purchases-by-category correctly drops a deleted bill's category; revenue-by-customer restores invoice outstanding to original amount after txn-delete cascade.
critical_code_review_comments: link_cascade._reverse_payment_impact duplicates logic already present inline in routes/transactions.py::_reverse_and_delete_payment (link endpoint). Consider consolidating both callers to use the new helper to keep balance-reversal math in one place.

cascade_on_doc_delete clears BOTH linked_payment_id and the doc-side field (linked_invoice_id/linked_bill_id) on the transaction — this is correct for cascade cleanup, but the transaction still retains category/posting; a stale-link audit query may be useful for future health checks.
cascade helpers do not write to audit ledger or emit AI-activity events; if that's expected for delete flows, wire it up alongside the cascade call.
seed_data_creation: Tests create temporary TEST-prefixed invoices/bills/txns/payments and clean them up in-flow.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend cascade behavior fully verified in /app/backend/tests/test_iter64_link_cascade.py. To run: `export REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=$(grep REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL /app/frontend/.env | cut -d= -f2) && pytest backend/tests/test_iter64_link_cascade.py -o addopts= -v`. Note the `-o addopts=` override — the repo's pytest.ini pins xdist which errored on unknown args; disabling addopts runs it serially cleanly.
rca of the issue: n/a — feature verification, no bugs found.
